key_insight: Tree-Ising repairs reasoning loops through sparse BF16 weight edits, outperforming an LLM-agent repair without gradients or LLM tokens.
engineering_relevance: Discrete weight optimization could make targeted model repairs cheaper and more bit-efficient, using four forward-pass requests and about $0.90 in GPU time for the annealing recipe.
method: Use forward statistics to weaken looping behavior, strengthen concluding behavior, and preserve outputs on productive tokens.
Restrict edits to admissible sign flips and exponent shifts while preserving shared group exponents and mantissas.
Decompose the objective into independent per-row QUBO problems, solved on GPU by simulated annealing or simulated bifurcation.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3.5-0.8B, Tree-Ising scores 54.6–55.1% on MATH-500 versus 51.7% for the agent edit; on Qwen3.5-2B, it raises greedy GSM8K accuracy from 21.6% to 69.4%.
watch_item: Evidence focuses on math benchmarks and two model sizes; broader capability preservation remains unestablished, and quantum execution covers only an eight-variable proof of concept.
paper_title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
